slides.text: In 1957, Disneyland’s Tomorrowland opened a house of the future, made almost entirely of plastic.
slides.kicker: Monsanto House of the Future · Anaheim

slides.text: Monsanto, a chemical company, paid for it to show what plastic could do. Two architects from MIT designed it.
Four plastic wings stretched sixteen feet out from a concrete core, with nothing underneath them.
Inside, it was set thirty years ahead, in 1986, with a microwave oven in the kitchen.
More than 20 million people walked through it in ten years.
In 1967, Tomorrowland was being redone, and the house had to come down.
The wrecking ball bounced off. Crews tried torches, chainsaws and jackhammers, then crushed it with chains.
The steel bolts holding it to the ground broke before the house did.
Its concrete foundation is still there, painted green and used as a planter.
